arxiv-2302-02279.title: Primal Characterizations of Stability of Error Bounds for Semi-infinite Convex Constraint Systems in Banach Spaces Thanks: Research of the first author was supported by the National Natural Science Foundations of China (Grant Nos. 11971422 and 12171419), and funded by Science and Technology Project
arxiv-2302-02279.creator: Zhou Wei, Michel Théra, Jen-Chih Yao
arxiv-2302-02279.description: Abstract This article is devoted to the stability of error bounds (local and global) for semi-infinite convex constraint systems in Banach spaces. We provide primal characterizations of the stability of local and global error bounds when systems are subject to small perturbations.

arxiv-2401-09681.title: Harnessing Density Ratios for Online Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2401-09681.creator: Philip Amortila, Dylan J. Foster, Nan Jiang, Ayush Sekhari, Tengyang Xie
arxiv-2401-09681.description: Abstract The theories of offline and online reinforcement learning, despite having evolved in parallel, have begun to show signs of the possibility for a unification, with algorithms and analysis techniques for one setting often having natural counterparts in the other.

arxiv-2403-08684.title: Bubble breakup probability in turbulent flows
arxiv-2403-08684.creator: Aliénor Rivière 1,2, Stéphane Perrard 2
arxiv-2403-08684.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Aliénor Rivière 1,2, Stéphane Perrard 2. Bubbles drive gas and chemical transfers in various industrial and geophysical contexts, in which flows are typically turbulent. As gas and chemical transfers are bubble size dependent, their quantification requires a prediction of bubble breakup.

arxiv-2406-19702.title: Vector AutoRegressive Moving Average Models: A Review
arxiv-2406-19702.creator: Marie-Christine Düker, David S. Matteson, Ruey S. Tsay, Ines Wilms
arxiv-2406-19702.description: Abstract Abstract. Vector AutoRegressive Moving Average (VARMA) models form a powerful and general model class for analyzing dynamics among multiple time series. While VARMA models encompass the Vector AutoRegressive (VAR) models, their popularity in empirical applications is dominated by the latter. Can this phenomenon be explained fully by the simplicity of VAR models?

plos-pone-0003817.title: The Major Surface-Associated Saccharides of Klebsiella pneumoniae Contribute to Host Cell Association
plos-pone-0003817.creator: Abigail Clements, Fabien Gaboriaud, Jérôme F. L. Duval et al.
plos-pone-0003817.description: PLOS ONE research article. Analysing the pathogenic mechanisms of a bacterium requires an understanding of the composition of the bacterial cell surface. The bacterial surface provides the first barrier against innate immune mechanisms as well as mediating attachment to cells/surfaces to resist clearance.

pmc-10593796.title: The enhanced cytotoxicity on breast cancer cells by Tanshinone I-induced photodynamic effect
pmc-10593796.creator: Chen Fengchao, Zhang Siya, Yan Tongtong, Wang Hongquan, Li Jie, Wang Qiang, Subhan Danish, Li Kun
pmc-10593796.description: Recently, natural photosensitizers, such as berberine, curcumin, riboflavin, and emodin, have received more and more attention in photodynamic therapy. Tanshinone I (TanI) is extracted from a traditional Chinese herb Danshen, and exhibits many physiological functions including antitumor. TanI is a photoactive phytocompounds, but no work was tried to investigate its potential photodynamic effect.

pmc-10655074.title: CircGUCY2C regulates cofilin 1 by sponging miR-425-3p to promote the proliferation of porcine skeletal muscle satellite cells
pmc-10655074.creator: Kunlong Qi, Yaqing Dou, Chenlei Li, Yingke Liu, Chenglei Song, Xinjian Li, Kejun Wang, Ruimin Qiao, Xiuling Li, Feng Yang, Xuelei Han
pmc-10655074.description: Circular ribonucleic acids (or circRNAs) are an emerging class of endogenous noncoding RNAs that are involved in physiological and pathological processes. Increasing evidence suggests that circRNAs play an important regulatory role in skeletal muscle development and meat quality regulation. In this study, it was found that circGUCY2C exhibits a high expression level in the longissimus dorsi muscle.

pmc-11498953.creator: Marziyeh Rajabi, Elahe Pourahmadi, Amin Adel, Asma Rashki Kemmak

pmc-11654344.title: Therapeutic potential of Indonesian plant extracts in combating malaria and protozoan neglected tropical disease
pmc-11654344.creator: Defi Kartika Sari, Ghulam Jeelani, Hilkatul Ilmi, Lidya Tumewu, Ratna Wahyuni, Aty Widyawaruyanti, Tomoyoshi Nozaki, Achmad Fuad Hafid
pmc-11654344.description: BackgroundNeglected tropical diseases (NTDs) afflict nearly 2 billion people worldwide and are caused by various pathogens, such as bacteria, protozoa, and trypanosoma, prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions. Among the 17 NTDs recognized by the World Health Organization (WHO), protozoal infections caused by Plasmodium, Entamoeba, Leishmania, and Trypanosoma are particularly prominent and pose significant public health.

pmc-11657688.title: Risk factors for hidden blood loss in unilateral biportal endoscopic lumbar interbody fusion : a single-center retrospective study
pmc-11657688.creator: Jian-fang Jin, Hao-ran Chen, Yu-jian Peng, Jun Dai, Qian-liang Wang, Jun Yan
pmc-11657688.description: BackgroundHidden blood loss (HBL) is often ignored unilateral biportal endoscopic interbody fusion surgery (ULIF). We investigated the amount and influencing factors of HBL in ULIF surgery in this study.MethodsFrom October 2020 to November 2023, 100 patients’ clinical and radiological data were retrospectively analyzed. Pearson or Spearman correlation and multivariate linear regression were used to identify factors linked to HBL.

pmc-12599213.title: Evaluation of Management Strategies for Viral Upper Respiratory Tract Infections Among Pediatricians in Türkiye
pmc-12599213.creator: Ismail Yildiz, Erdem Gonullu, Utkucan Uckun, Ibrahim Kandemir, Ahmet Soysal, Metin Karabocuoglu
pmc-12599213.description: BackgroundTo evaluate how pediatricians manage viral upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) in children and their tendencies about the viral URTIs approaches.Materials and MethodsThis study was conducted among pediatricians who participated in a descriptive cross-sectional survey. The survey included pediatricians who were willing to participate and who completed the survey forms between June 2023 and February 2024.

pmc-12660296.title: EXO1 overexpression induces homologous recombination deficiency and enhances PARP inhibitor sensitivity in ER-positive breast cancer: modulation by N4BP2L2-Mediated restoration
pmc-12660296.creator: Runa Sugiyama, Anna S. Sedukhina, Eri Sato, Ayako Yamaura, Kimino Minagawa, Sookhee Pae, Ena Imai, Ankita Chawla, Ziran Xu, Mihika Chakraborty, Satori Gonoi, Jotaro Yamaoka, Kazuo Yudo, Koichiro Tsugawa, Ko Sato
pmc-12660296.description: Exonuclease 1 (EXO1) is a critical enzyme in homologous recombination (HR) and is implicated in cancer progression, with overexpression linked to poor prognosis in multiple tumor types. Yet, the impact of EXO1 overexpression on HR efficiency in estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer remains unclear.

pmc-12734636.title: Review of the Relationship Between the Composition, Strength, and Ultimate Tensile Strain of Engineering Geopolymer Composites
pmc-12734636.creator: Xiaomei Wan, Weili Guo, Jiahao Cong, Chen Wang, Mingjin Han
pmc-12734636.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Engineered Geopolymer Composites (EGC) combine the high ductility and multi-crack characteristics of traditional Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC) with the sound low-carbon advantages of geopolymers, making them a research hotspot in the green high-performance materials. This study focuses on the influence of EGC composition (precursor, activator, fiber and fine aggregate) on its tensile properties and the curing regime for different precursor compositions. The reported results data (with ultimate tensile strain exceeding 2%) from recent EGC studies are collected and reviewed.

pmc-13242503.title: A Dataset of Widefield Fundus Images From Patients With Birdshot Chorioretinitis and Matched Control
pmc-13242503.creator: Thomas Foulonneau, Caroline Memmi, Dominique Monnet, Antoine P Brézin, Aliénor Vienne-Jumeau
pmc-13242503.description: Birdshot chorioretinitis is a rare uveitis where research is limited by the lack of large, publicly available imaging datasets. To address this gap, we present Birdshot-Wide, a standardized retinal imaging dataset comprising 5,042 widefield fundus photographs from 742 eyes with birdshot chorioretinitis (BSCR) and 1,310 images from 742 age-and sex- matched healthy eyes controls.

pmc-13574587.title: County-level variation and trajectories in ADHD medication dispensing among Norwegian children and adolescents, 2005-2022: a nationwide prescription register study
pmc-13574587.creator: Espen Anker, Bothild Bendiksen, Gro Janne Wergeland, Per Hove Thomsen
pmc-13574587.description: BackgroundNational trends in ADHD medication use in Norway have recently been described. Less is known about whether children and adolescents in different counties have followed similar or diverging medication-dispensing trajectories over time. We therefore examined county-level variation and county-level trajectories in ADHD medication dispensing among Norwegian children and adolescents from 2005 to 2022.
